description:
Found s395 while fixing #314 family F-B.  With `our $count++` lowering,
op/inccode.t COMPILES (TRANSPILE-FAIL -> runs) but dies at its test 2:

    crash: The value #<function (lambda (&rest %_args) ...)> is not of type ...

That file is `# Tests for the coderef-in-@INC feature` end to end (89 perl
rows), so the whole remaining gap is one feature: an @INC element that is not
a directory string.  Perl accepts three hook shapes there and PCL accepts none:

  1. a CODE ref            -- called as $hook->($hook, $filename)
  2. an ARRAY ref whose [0] is a coderef (called with the array as $hook)
  3. a blessed object with an INC method -- $hook->INC($filename)

The hook returns, in order of preference: a filehandle to read the module
source from, a coderef generating lines, or a (filehandle, coderef) pair; an
undef/empty return means "not found, keep searching @INC".

LAYER: this is `require`'s search loop -- genuine core semantics, so the
runtime (the module loader in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp), NOT a lib/ shim.  The
interaction to settle first is PCL's module CACHE: a hook-produced source has
no stable path key, so it must not be cached under one.

BAR: probe each of the three hook shapes against perl (return-a-filehandle and
return-a-coderef); re-run op/inccode.t and op/inccode-tie.t (the tie variant is
separately blocked on "multiple package sections" in string eval) and splice
their snapshot rows; gate; corpus-diff (expect identical -- a runtime change
makes the full sweep NON-OPTIONAL, s377 rule).
subject: coderef-in-@INC hooks unsupported - op/inccode.t compiles but dies at test 2 (89 rows)
